## A production-minded AI practice, not a hype machine.

URL: https://arithim.com/about.html

ABOUT ARITHIM

# A production-minded AI practice, not a hype machine.

Arithim is a London software company. We make enterprise software and SaaS products, and we help energy, industrial, telecoms, and regulated businesses put practical AI into the workflows they already run.

HOW WE THINK

Practical AI should be explainable, auditable, and built into real workflows. We would rather ship one system a team trusts than ten demos nobody uses.

### Operations first

We map the real workflow before proposing a model. The system has to fit how you actually work.

### Explainable by default

Every decision the system makes can be traced, audited, and defended. No black boxes in regulated settings.

### Built to be handed over

We leave you with operating models and training, not a dependency on us to keep the lights on.

FOUNDER

## Tarun Bulchandani

Applied AI & operational systems, London

Tarun founded Arithim to close the gap between AI potential and operational reality. With a background spanning enterprise systems, SAP ERP environments, and regulated industry workflows, he builds AI that survives contact with real operations, where auditability, integration, and trust matter more than novelty.

FREQUENTLY ASKED

## Questions about our products

Which Arithim products can I try or buy now?

Site Finder is available now, with reports and subscriptions ordered by email. The Technical Sales Guide runs as demos and pilots. Find Me A Job and Unrejectable are live. The AI model inventory and three of the data products are in early access, and two more are planned.

What is the difference between enterprise software, data products and SaaS?

Enterprise software is set up for each customer on their own data, starting with a demo or a pilot. Data products give you sourced answers on a site, a grid connection, a planning risk or a company, as a report or through an API. SaaS products are the same for everyone, and you sign up on their website.

Does Arithim build software for clients too?

Yes. We also take on AI readiness work, automation, SAP ERP reporting, websites, training and regulatory systems for clients. The services page has the details.

## Every salesperson answers like your best technical manager.

URL: https://arithim.com/technical-sales-guide.html

TECHNICAL SALES GUIDE · FOR CHEMICAL AND INGREDIENT DISTRIBUTORS

# Every salesperson answers like your best technical manager.

Your reps ask for a product by application and condition, in animal nutrition, coatings, construction chemicals or another industry you sell into. They get a ranked answer with cost in use, landed cost and the registrations that apply in each country, without waiting for the technical manager. The interface and the website concierge work in Arabic.

Request a demo →See what it does

Describe this animation

Three examples play in turn. In animal nutrition, a rep asks for a heat-stress product for broilers in Saudi Arabia. In coatings, a dispersant for a water-based wall paint in the UAE. In construction chemicals, a superplasticiser for ready-mix concrete poured in a Riyadh summer. Each time, three products from three principals appear in ranked order with dose, cost in use and landed cost, the sources are listed, and Replace swaps in a competitor equivalent with the saving shown. All figures are samples.

WHAT IT DOES

## What can the Technical Sales Guide do for a distributor?

Technical answers sit with a few managers and in folders of PDFs. These are the six jobs the Guide takes off their desks, each shown with sample figures. You can pause any of the animations.

### How do I find the right product for an application and condition?

Name the application and the condition, such as heat stress in broilers. Your rep sees which products fit best, from every supplier in your range, with the numbers needed to quote beside each one.

Dose, cost in use and landed cost beside each product, so the rep can quote on the spot.

Competitor equivalents, and Replace for when a supply line fails or a customer asks for another brand.

A rep at a Saudi broiler mill asks for a heat-stress solution and gets products from three principals, ranked.

Describe this animation

A rep types an application and condition. Three products from three principals appear in ranked order with dose, cost in use per tonne of feed and landed cost, and the sources are listed underneath. A competitor equivalent is found and Replace swaps Principal A for Principal C, saving $0.40 per tonne of feed. All figures are samples.

### How do I answer a customer's technical question from our principals' documents?

Add the data sheets, safety data sheets and certificates your principals send. Reps ask in plain words and get the answer with the document and page it came from, so a technical manager can confirm it quickly.

The matching lines are highlighted on the page.

Certificates and documents carry expiry dates, and the owner is reminded before they lapse.

Details taken from a document, such as moisture or shelf life, go on a product page only after a person has approved them.

A technical manager uploads a principal's data sheet and asks for the maximum inclusion rate in layer feed. The answer points to page 3.

Describe this animation

A PDF data sheet is added and opens at page 1. A question about layer inclusion rates is typed. The answer appears with a citation to page 3 and the matching lines are highlighted. An expiry alert and an extraction waiting for review follow. All figures are samples.

### Which of our products are registered where, and what expires next?

Each product and country has a registration record with the holder, the number, the expiry date and the document checklist. The owner is reminded before anything lapses.

Rules and key dates per country, with the products and customers each one affects.

A record per product and country: holder, number, expiry and documents.

An expiry reminder that becomes a renewal task.

A registration in Saudi Arabia is 60 days from expiry. The regulatory team gets an alert and a renewal task, and sales sees which customers buy the product.

Describe this animation

A table of registrations by product and country. One row for Saudi Arabia turns amber at 60 days. An alert appears, a renewal task is created with a checklist in which one document is missing, and three customers who buy the product are listed. All figures are samples.

### How do I show a principal where its products win and lose?

Principals log in to a live view of their own products: what you proposed, won and lost, and why. The review packs you already produce for each principal by country become a screen the principal opens whenever it likes.

Wins, losses and recorded loss reasons by country and product.

Each principal sees its own products and nothing else.

The competitor is named where the rep recorded it.

A principal's regional manager opens the portal and sees wins, losses and loss reasons without asking for a report.

Describe this animation

A principal portal limited to one principal's products. Counts of proposals, wins and losses rise. Bars show results by country and reasons for lost deals. A note says a competitor was named on five of nine losses. All figures are samples.

### How do I turn website visitors' questions into leads for the right team?

A product advisor on your website answers visitors from your catalogue and your principals' documents. When a visitor wants to talk to a person, it takes their details and sends the lead to the right team.

Visitors ask in their own language, including Arabic.

Leads arrive with the product, application and place already filled in.

You see what visitors ask for most, and the gaps in your range.

A visitor asks in Arabic about heat stress in broilers, agrees to be contacted, and becomes a lead routed to the Eastern Province team.

Describe this animation

A chat on a website. The visitor writes in Arabic about heat stress in broilers, with an English gloss under each line. The advisor answers with a source and offers a contact from the Eastern Province team. The visitor agrees, and a lead card shows the interest, language and place. All figures are samples.

### How do I produce a co-branded data sheet or application guide without starting from a blank page?

Choose a document type and the Guide drafts it from your catalogue and library, in your branding or with the principal's.

Branded and co-branded data sheets, application guides and comparison sheets.

Regulatory statements that use the registration details on file.

Draft content for your website.

Every draft goes to a person for review before it is used.

A marketing lead produces a data sheet with the principal's logo beside the distributor's, with dose, shelf life and registration filled in from the record.

Describe this animation

A data sheet template is chosen with co-branding and an English option. A page builds up with two logos, a title, specification rows, a registration line and a sources footer. An export button and a draft-for-review status follow. All figures are samples.

Try these jobs on your own product range.

Request a demo →

ALSO IN THE PRODUCT

## What else helps the sales team day to day?

Around the six main jobs: a light CRM, training for new reps, a way to flag wrong answers, offline briefs, product data you can rely on and feed formulation tools.

### Can we keep accounts and opportunities in the Guide without replacing our CRM?

Yes. The Guide has a light CRM for technical selling, with accounts, opportunities and territories. Import them from Dynamics 365 or Salesforce with ready-made settings, and keep the two in step through the API.

Sales roles see the territories they cover.

A lost deal needs a reason, and the reasons feed the principal review packs.

A sales manager imports accounts from Dynamics 365, then records why a betaine deal at a feed mill was lost and which competitor won it.

Describe this animation

A Dynamics 365 export is imported with ready-made settings, and counts show 128 accounts, 46 opportunities and 4 territories. One opportunity turns amber as lost. A form asks for the reason, price against a competitor, and the competitor is named. A note says the reason goes into the principal review pack. All figures are samples.

### How do new reps learn our range and the rules that apply?

Short learning paths take a new rep through the range, the applications and the rules, one module at a time, and each module ends with a quiz.

A rep in their second week finishes the enzymes module and gets four of five quiz questions right.

Describe this animation

A learning path of five modules shows two done, one in progress and two to go. A quiz question asks what phytase releases from feed, and the correct answer, phosphorus bound in phytate, is ticked. A note shows four of five correct so far. All content is a sample.

### What happens when an answer is wrong?

Anyone can flag an answer with one click and say what looks wrong. Flagged answers are reviewed each working day and corrected.

Each answer shows where it came from: a supplier source, an expert draft or a confirmed review.

A rep spots a dose that looks high against the new data sheet, flags it, and sees it corrected after review.

Describe this animation

An answer gives a layer feed dose of 4,000 grams per tonne, citing an older data sheet. The rep presses Flag this answer and types that the new sheet says 2,000. A note says it went to today's review. The corrected answer then shows 2,000 grams per tonne citing the newer sheet. All figures are samples.

### Can reps use it at a plant with no signal?

Yes. Save an account brief before a plant visit and it opens without a connection. Saved briefs are removed from the device when the person signs out.

A rep saves the brief for a broiler integrator's plant in Dammam and opens it on site with no signal.

Describe this animation

A brief marked as saved for offline use shows the plant, the products the customer buys, an open opportunity, the last visit and registration status. A notice says there is no signal but the brief still opens, and a note says the brief is removed from the device at sign-out. All content is a sample.

### How do we keep product data complete and consistent?

Each product has one passport page with a completeness score. Gaps and possible duplicates are called out, and the same facts reach your website, CRM and ERP.

A product manager sees a xylanase blend at 78% complete, fills in the shelf life and merges a duplicate entry.

Describe this animation

A product passport shows a completeness bar rising to 78%. Two gaps are listed, shelf life and an Arabic product name, and one check passes. A possible duplicate is flagged for merging. Chips show the passport feeding the website, CRM and ERP. All figures are samples.

### Can the Guide help with feed formulation?

Two tools help a rep or nutritionist talk numbers with a customer: feed savings worked out from enzyme matrix values, and a mycotoxin risk advisor. Both are a starting point for a nutritionist to confirm.

A rep shows a broiler mill how much phosphate phytase can replace, and what that saves per tonne after the enzyme cost.

Describe this animation

A broiler grower feed with phytase at 500 FTU per kilogram. A table shows dicalcium phosphate falling from 12 to 6 kilograms per tonne and limestone from 9 to 7. The saving is $3.10 per tonne, or $1.95 net of enzyme cost. A risk panel then shows aflatoxin high and fumonisin low for maize from one origin. All figures are samples.

SECURITY AND TRUST

## Is the Technical Sales Guide secure enough for our principals' data?

What was in place on 22 October 2026. The security page has every answer in full, including what is still to come, and your security team can ask for the questionnaire answers and the data processing agreement.

### Each customer's data is separate

Each customer's data is kept apart from every other customer's, and only people in your company can see it.

### No passwords

People sign in with an emailed link or a one-time code. A company can require two-step sign-in for its administrators or for everyone.

### A record of who did what

Administrators can see changes, imports, exports and sign-ins.

### Hosted in Frankfurt

The application and its data are hosted in Frankfurt, as of 22 October 2026.

### AI is off by default

Arithim does not currently send customer data to an AI provider. A provider would be added to the sub-processor list with 30 days' notice first.

### Not yet certified

We are preparing for ISO/IEC 27001. Single sign-on and an independent penetration test are not available yet.

### How will I know an answer is right?

Each answer shows where it came from, and anyone can flag one that looks wrong. Flagged answers are reviewed and corrected each working day. Treat a ranking as a starting point for a technical person to confirm.

FREQUENTLY ASKED

## Questions about the Technical Sales Guide

How can my sales team answer technical questions without calling our technical manager?

The Technical Sales Guide lets a salesperson answer a customer's technical question without calling a specialist. It holds a catalogue of 466 products from 147 suppliers across 8 industries. Your rep asks by application and condition and sees the products ranked, with dose, cost in use and landed cost, competitor equivalents and substitutes, and the regulations and registrations that apply. It is a starting point for a technical person to confirm.

How is this different from Copilot or ChatGPT over our SharePoint?

A chat assistant over a document folder can quote a data sheet. The Guide adds what a folder does not hold: products from many suppliers and their competitors side by side, a ranking by performance for an application, cost in use and landed cost, and registrations per product and country. Answers show where they came from, and flagged answers are reviewed each working day.

Does it work with Copilot?

You can keep Copilot for chat over your own files. The Guide adds ranked, cross-supplier answers with cost and registrations, and other tools can request its rankings through the REST API. There is no Copilot connector yet.

Does it work in Arabic?

The interface is available in ten languages, including Arabic, which displays right to left. The website concierge takes questions in Arabic. Product and catalogue content is in English today.

Can a principal see our data?

A principal sees a live view of its own products only: where they were proposed, won and lost, and the reasons recorded. It does not see other principals or the rest of your pipeline. You decide who gets access.

Does it connect to Dynamics 365 or Salesforce?

You can import accounts and opportunities from Dynamics 365 and Salesforce using ready-made import settings. A REST API with scoped keys and signed webhooks lets you keep accounts and opportunities in step with a CRM or ERP, read the catalogue and request rankings.

How do I know the answers are right?

Every answer shows where it came from, such as a supplier source, an expert draft or a confirmed review. Anyone can flag an answer that looks wrong, and flagged answers are reviewed each working day and corrected. Registration expiries remind the person who owns them.

How do we get started, and what does it cost?

Request a demo. Arithim sets up each customer directly, so there is no self-service sign-up. A pilot runs for eight weeks on one division in one country, using your principals' products and your team's real questions. Pricing depends on the modules and the number of users, and we give you a figure in the demo conversation.

## Is the Technical Sales Guide secure enough for our principals' data?

URL: https://arithim.com/technical-sales-guide-security.html

TECHNICAL SALES GUIDE · SECURITY AND TRUST

# Is the Technical Sales Guide secure enough for our principals' data?

These answers describe what was in place on 22 October 2026, and what was still to come. Your security team can ask for the questionnaire answers and the data processing agreement at security@arithim.com.

## Security questions and answers

Is my data separate from other customers?

Each customer's data is separated inside the database by row-level security. It is enabled and enforced on every table that holds customer data. Arithim audited all 106 tables on 19 October 2026.

People are limited by role, and sales roles are limited by territory. There are six roles.

How do people sign in?

There are no passwords in the product. People sign in with an emailed link or a one-time code. Two-step sign-in with an authenticator app is available, and a company can require it for its administrators or for everyone. The default is optional.

Each company can set an idle timeout and a maximum session length. People can sign out of every device, and administrators can end a person's sessions.

Can I see who did what?

Administrators can see an activity log of changes, imports, exports, sign-in events and security changes for their company, and export it. The application cannot edit or delete the log, and each entry is chained to the one before it, so tampering is detectable.

How do the API and webhooks protect data?

Administrators create API keys with scopes and an expiry. Keys are stored only as hashes, and a key stops working when its creator leaves, is demoted or is deactivated. Webhook calls are signed with HMAC-SHA256, sent only to https addresses, and blocked from reaching private network addresses.

How is the application itself secured?

Database queries use bound parameters, and user text is rendered as text. CSV exports neutralise spreadsheet formula injection. The only file uploads are CSV or text files for import, which are read and not stored.

Arithim reviewed the whole codebase for security on 19 October 2026 and fixed the findings in code. That was an internal review, not an independent penetration test. The codebase has an automated test suite of more than 200 test files, including tests for tenant isolation and access rules.

Where is my data hosted, and who processes it?

The application runs in Vercel's Frankfurt region (fra1) and the database is Supabase in Frankfurt (eu-central-1), as of 22 October 2026. Arithim acts as a processor for customer personal data, offers a data processing agreement, and gives 30 days' notice of changes to this list.

Sub-processorPurposeData it receives

SupabaseDatabase, sign-in and sessionsAll customer data

VercelHosting and server functionsRequests and responses, application logs

OpenStreetMap NominatimAddress search when a place is addedAddress text only

Google Maps PlatformOptional address search, off by defaultAddress text only

Is my data sent to an AI provider?

AI features are optional and off until a customer turns them on. Arithim does not currently send customer data to an AI provider. Before it does, the provider is added to the published sub-processor list with 30 days' notice. When AI drafting is used, its output is a proposal that a person approves before anything is saved.

What happens to my data over time?

Companies can set retention periods, and the system deletes data past them each day. Administrators can export and erase a person's data. On request, Arithim exports a company's data.

What policies and incident plan do you have?

Arithim has written security, access control, data protection, incident response, continuity, secure development and supplier policies, available to customers under NDA. The incident response plan has a target of telling affected customers within 24 hours of confirming an incident. The plan has not yet been rehearsed.

Are you ISO 27001 certified?

Not yet. Arithim is preparing the Technical Sales Guide for ISO/IEC 27001 certification and is not yet certified.

Not yet available: single sign-on for enterprise identity providers, and an independent penetration test.

Where do I report a vulnerability or ask for the data processing agreement?

Email security@arithim.com. Ask there for the DPA, the sub-processor list and the policy pack.

Request a demo and the security pack →Back to the Technical Sales Guide

## Screen sites for grid and planning risk before you pay for surveys.

SITE FINDER · SOLAR, BATTERY AND WIND IN GREAT BRITAIN

# Screen sites for grid and planning risk before you pay for surveys.

Say what you want to build: solar, battery storage, solar with a battery, or onshore wind. Site Finder ranks land across England, Scotland and Wales by grid headroom, planning record and project economics, so you know which sites deserve a visit and can show your investment committee why.

Book a demo →See prices and orderWatch it in use

Landowner check £195 · Feasibility report £1,950 · Portfolio screen £7,500 · Platform from £30,000 a year

Prices ex VAT. Order by email and pay by invoice.

Describe this animation

A question is typed: where should we build next? Chips show the project as 50 MWp, auto connection, CfD and a 6.5% hurdle. A verdict box says 8 of the top 20 sites are deliverable. A hex map fills in and a ranked list follows. Ellerstoke in Wendmoor needs £56.4 against a CfD price of £65.23, Kinlarrow in Glenmorvie needs £60.1, and Llanbedwyn in Dyffryn Cerwen needs £59.2. Numbered markers place the sites on the map. Names and figures are made up to show the interface.

WHO IT IS FOR

## Who uses Site Finder?

Developers, funds and landowners who need to decide where to spend time and money.

### Developer land and origination teams

Find the sites most likely to connect and get consent, and take the shortlist to your investment committee with the evidence attached. Your team makes unlimited landowner checks and feasibility reports.

Site Finder platform, from £30,000 a year →

### Fund and acquisition analysts

Test a seller's pipeline before you pay for it. Each claim is marked confirmed, contradicted, not verifiable or seller-supplied, with a data-room PDF and Excel workbook.

Portfolio screen, £7,500 for up to 50 sites →

### Landowners and land agents

Had a letter from a developer? See what the land looks like, how crowded the nearest grid point is, who the developer is, what else they hold nearby and any pressure terms in the letter.

Landowner check, £195 →

### First-time developers and consultants

Get a verdict on one site with the reasons: the grid and planning position, the economics and the source behind each number.

Site feasibility report, £1,950 →

Site Finder narrows where to look. Your team still visits the land, talks to the network operator and takes planning advice.

FOR EVERY SITE

## What will I know about a site before I visit?

Every site opens into four answers you can take to a land agent, a network operator or your committee.

### Can it connect?

The nearest substations, the headroom the network operator publishes, whether the site is likely to fit the current Gate 2 window, and who else already holds capacity there.

### Will it get consent?

Schemes built, consented and refused nearby, how the local authority has decided similar applications, and the likely consent route for the size of your project.

### Does it make money?

An indicative connection cost, the price per MWh the site needs to reach your hurdle rate, and how that moves when your assumptions change. For batteries, the break-even capex with and without the export credit.

### Can we defend it?

A constraint checklist and the source behind every number. Any site can go into a feasibility report, a grid pack, an investment committee pack or an Excel model.

BEYOND THE MAP

## What can I do once I have a shortlist?

Keep working the shortlist: track each site to energisation, watch what other developers are doing and check a seller's claims.

### Screen your own sites

Upload a boundary, a KML or a shapefile, or draw one on the map, and see how it compares with the ranked list.

### Track every site to energisation

A pipeline board shows how firm each site's connection evidence is, from map only to energised, with reminders for Gate 2 milestones and land-rights deadlines.

### See who holds the grid

A company group's projects and connections by technology, stage, substation and planning authority, plus Gate 2 positions with no planning application and connections that sit idle.

### Hear about competitor moves

New connection applications, Gate changes, status moves and holder changes for the companies, substations and areas you watch, in the app and in a weekly email.

### Check a seller's pipeline

Import a seller's site list and see each claim marked confirmed, contradicted, not verifiable or seller-supplied, with a data-room PDF and Excel workbook.

### "Can I build here?"

Three guided checks: for a landowner approached by a developer, for a developer weighing one site, and for an investor testing a pipeline. Each ends with a one-page summary and questions for an adviser.

### Know the rules

Dated cards on the consent route by nation and size, Gate 2 milestones and battery fire-safety guidance.

### Feed your own tools and AI assistants

Through the data API and MCP server, your tools and assistants can read projects, substations, map cells, company holdings and changes.

SEE IT IN USE

## What does Site Finder look like in use?

Animated scenes of the interface. The names and figures are made up to show how the tool works. They are not results for any project.

### A working session

#### Ask the question and read the answer

Load the app, read the verdict and scan the ranked list, then look across the map of scored sites.

Describe this animation

A question is typed: where should we build next? Chips show the project as 50 MWp, auto connection, CfD and a 6.5% hurdle. A verdict box says 8 of the top 20 sites are deliverable. A hex map fills in and a ranked list follows. Ellerstoke in Wendmoor needs £56.4 against a CfD price of £65.23, Kinlarrow in Glenmorvie needs £60.1, and Llanbedwyn in Dyffryn Cerwen needs £59.2. Numbered markers place the sites on the map. Names and figures are made up to show the interface.

#### Open the evidence for a site

Open the top site: its score breakdown, substations, planning record and economics, then the one-page print pack.

Describe this animation

The top row, Ellerstoke in Wendmoor, is selected and an evidence drawer slides up. Six bars grow for grid, planning, solar and terrain, economics, deliverability and environment. Cards then show the nearest substation, Carrowby East Grid 33kV at 0.7 km with capacity ok, the planning record, and the economics: the site needs £56.4 against a CfD price of £65.23. Names and figures are made up to show the interface.

#### Push back and see what changed

Mark a substation as full and rescore, read the What changed card, then assume a Gate 2 offer and watch the answer move.

Describe this animation

Four ranked sites sit above a card for the substation Carrowby East Grid 33kV. Challenge is pressed, the substation is marked full, and a note says the operator has no spare capacity. After Rescore the rows move. Ellerstoke falls from first to fourth and the other three each rise one place. A What changed card lists each move and names the override as the cause. Names and figures are made up to show the interface.

### Features up close

#### Gate 2 and grid headroom

See which sites can connect in the current window, then assume a Gate 2 offer and watch the ranking move.

Describe this animation

A bar shows 127.3 MW of Gate 2 solar capacity left in a zone. Three ranked sites of 38 MWac each take their share in rank order, and the figure falls to 89.3, 51.3 and then 13.3 MW. The fourth site, Daverby Magna, needs 36 MWac. It does not fit, so it moves to a box marked needs next window, with a later energisation year. Names and figures are made up to show the interface.

#### Planning record by local authority

Search the planning record by local authority for decisions, approval rates and recent schemes.

Describe this animation

A table lists local authorities, with a bar for the share of solar schemes approved. Saltmere is selected. Its panel says it approved 10 of 11 solar schemes since 2019, with a median decision time of 8 months, and a small chart shows decisions per year. A note says the rate is the authority's record and does not predict the outcome for a specific scheme. Names and figures are made up to show the interface.

#### Refused schemes nearby

A refused solar scheme near a site lowers its score, and the site's evidence names the scheme.

Describe this animation

A score waterfall for a site at Fennick Green in Callowfield starts at 0.84 before flags. Three multipliers follow: 0.91 for a refused scheme 1.7 km away, 0.94 for a National Park or AONB setting, and 0.92 for a listed building. The score ends at 0.66. A small map then shows the site, a dashed 1.7 km line and the refused scheme, Fallowmere Solar Farm, 34.5 MW. Names and figures are made up to show the interface.

#### Economics and project size

Take the project size past 100 MWac and watch the consent route, transmission charges and NPV change.

Describe this animation

A slider for project size moves from 90 to 110 MWac. As it passes 100 MWac the consent route changes from the local planning authority to the NSIP Development Consent Order route, and the NPV falls from +£7.6m to −£0.4m. A note names the size threshold and both values. Names and figures are made up to show the interface.

PUSH BACK

## What if my team disagrees with the ranking?

Change what you believe about the market and the ranking follows, so the answer reflects your view.

### Test your own assumptions

Change the technology, project size, revenue route, capex and hurdle rate. Draw areas on the map to include or exclude, or mark a single substation as full and note why.

### See what moved and why

After each change, a card lists the sites that entered or left the top of the list, how far each moved and which assumption caused it.

### Share the scenario

Save a set of assumptions under a name, compare two side by side and send one to a colleague as a link.

LIMITS

## What does Site Finder not cover?

Site Finder screens sites. It does not replace a network operator's connection offer, planning advice or a site visit, and its connection costs are estimates for comparing sites. Where a network operator publishes no headroom, the site is marked unknown. Aerodrome and Ministry of Defence safeguarding is not assessed, so check it with the aerodrome operator, the MoD safeguarding team and, for wind, the NATS self-assessment maps before you commit. Coverage is Great Britain, and Site Finder does not show who owns a particular field.

FREQUENTLY ASKED

## Questions buyers ask about Site Finder

How does Site Finder help me find sites?

Tell it what you want to build and it ranks land across England, Scotland and Wales, with the grid, planning and economics behind each rank. Your team can spend survey money on sites that already look viable.

Which technologies and areas does it cover?

Solar, battery storage, solar with battery on a shared connection, and onshore wind, across Great Britain. Northern Ireland is not covered.

Does it replace a grid connection offer or planning advice?

No. It narrows where to look. Connection costs are indicative, so a network operator quote will differ, and planning advice, a site visit and aerodrome or Ministry of Defence checks still come before you commit.

Can it tell me whether a site can connect soon?

Where the network operator publishes a headroom figure, Site Finder shows it with its date, and where it does not, the site is marked unknown. It also shows who already holds capacity at the substation, and you can assume a Gate 2 offer and see how the ranking changes.

Can I test my own assumptions?

Yes. Change the technology, project size, revenue route, capex or hurdle rate, or mark a substation as full. The ranking updates and a card lists which sites moved and why.

How much does Site Finder cost?

Prices exclude VAT. A landowner check is £195 a report. A site feasibility report is £1,950 a site, and the solar and battery hybrid add-on is £500 on top. A portfolio screen is £7,500 for up to 50 sites and £120 for each extra site. The Site Finder platform is from £30,000 a year for 5 seats, Market Watch from £15,000 a year, and the data API and MCP from £18,000 a year. Enterprise terms are on quote.

How do I order, and how long does a report take?

Press Order on the product in the pricing section. Your email app opens a message to tarun@arithim.com with the product in the subject and the details we need listed in the body. We confirm the order by email and invoice after confirmation. A landowner check and a site feasibility report each take 3 working days, a hybrid add-on comes with its feasibility report, and a portfolio screen takes 5 working days. Orders are subject to our terms, sent with the invoice.

Who is Site Finder for, and can I see a demo first?

Developers and their land teams, funds and acquisition analysts, landowners and land agents, and first-time developers and consultants. Book a demo and we run Site Finder on a brief you choose: the technology, the project size, how you want to connect and the regions you care about.

GOOD TO KNOW

## Before you start

The report states what it covered, what it did not and how confident we are in each finding. It is an attestation, not a guarantee about every system in your company.

Some use cannot be seen from company systems, such as AI on personal devices. The report says so.

A model that runs inside a supplier's own service can only be confirmed with the supplier's help. Where it cannot be, the report marks it open.

It does not need to see your prompts or your customers' data.

It is not a legal opinion on whether a rule applies to you.

FREQUENTLY ASKED

## Questions about AI model inventory

What is an AI model inventory?

A current list of the AI models your business uses, in your products, your systems and your suppliers' services, with where each runs, who owns it and whether it is approved.

Is this the same as AI security posture management, shadow AI discovery or a CASB?

Those tools watch and control how AI is used. This answers a different question: which models are in use, and can you prove it. It can sit alongside them.

Why not just ask teams and suppliers?

You should, and we help you structure the questions. Answers from people are incomplete and go out of date quickly, and a questionnaire is not evidence. The inventory gives you something to check them against.

Does it find shadow AI?

It looks for AI use that is not on your approved list, across the areas we agree in scope, and says what it could not see.

Does it cover AI inside our suppliers' products?

Where it shows up in your own estate and with the supplier's help. Where it cannot be confirmed, the report marks it open and suggests the question to put to the supplier.

Do you need agents on our endpoints or changes to our network?

We agree what access is needed before we start. We aim to work from what you already have, with read-only access, and we do not sit in the path of your live traffic.

Does it read our prompts or customer data?

No. It does not need to.

Can it show open models running on our own GPUs?

Yes, if you want that in scope.

Does it help with ISO 42001, the NIST AI RMF, the EU AI Act or customer questionnaires?

It gives you the factual inventory those frameworks and questionnaires ask for. It does not certify compliance and it is not legal advice.

Which models can it flag, for example DeepSeek?

Whichever your policy rules out. Governments and customers have started naming particular models, and we flag whatever you list.

Is the report a certificate?

No. It is an attestation report that states its scope and date and says what we found in that scope. It does not claim to prove that nothing ruled out exists anywhere in your company.

How do we know the answer is complete?

The report says what was covered, what was not and our confidence in each finding. Where it is partial, we tell you, and we tell you what would close the gap.

Do UK firms have to keep an AI model inventory?

Not by a single UK rule that we can point to. Customers, suppliers and risk teams are asking the question, and frameworks such as ISO 42001 expect a register of AI in use. We will tell you if you do not need it.

How long does it take, and what does it cost?

We scope it with you first, agree a first milestone, then quote.

## Need a straight answer on which AI you run?

Tell us what you need to show and to whom. We will tell you what the inventory would cover and whether it is worth doing.

Month-end reporting takes less manual effort, repetitive SAP steps done by hand can be automated, and your core system is not replaced or changed.

# Find Me A Job

An AI job-search product that does the searching for you. It reads a candidate's profile, matches it against live listings across the market and returns the roles worth applying to.

TYPE

Owned product

DOMAIN

Careers & recruitment AI

STATUS

Live

THE PROBLEM

Job seekers drown in near-duplicate listings spread across dozens of boards. Search is keyword-shallow, relevance is low, and the effort of filtering good roles from noise falls entirely on the candidate. Most people give up long before they run out of suitable jobs.

HOW IT WORKS

The candidate describes themselves once. A matching engine reads live listings, scores each against the profile for fit and realistic chance, ranks what's left and hands back a short list instead of another endless feed.

PROFILE

RANK

SHORTLIST

Find Me A Job turns a demoralising scroll into a short list of roles a person can actually act on. It's a working example of Arithim's thesis: AI is most useful when it removes effort from a decision people already have to make.

"Fewer, better matches beat an infinite feed every time."

# Unrejectable

An AI tool that tests a job application before anyone at the employer sees it. It reads a CV and application the way a screener does, then tells the candidate what to fix to get past the first cut.

TYPE

Owned product

DOMAIN

Careers & recruitment AI

STATUS

Live

THE PROBLEM

HOW IT WORKS

DRAFT

ANALYSE

REWRITE

INTERVIEW

Unrejectable moves the feedback loop to before the rejection, where it can still change the outcome. It's the companion product to Find Me A Job: one finds the right roles, and the other works on the application.

## Designing Websites for AI Discoverability

URL: https://arithim.com/insight-designing-websites-for-ai-discoverability.html

Insights / AI discoverability

# Designing Websites for AI Discoverability

AI DISCOVERABILITY·12 JAN 2026·2 MIN READ·BY TARUN BULCHANDANI

Modern websites are read by people, search engines, and AI systems. That changes the role of structure.

Clear headings, semantic HTML, accessible relationships, schema markup, internal links, and explicit entity signals all help machines understand what a company does and why it matters. None of it is exotic; most of it is just doing the fundamentals properly.

This is not a trick for ranking. It is an information architecture discipline.

A website should make the organisation legible: its services, expertise, evidence, operating context, and contact pathways. If a person or a model reads one page, they should come away knowing what you do and who it is for.

AI discoverability starts with the same fundamentals that make a website better for humans: clarity, hierarchy, and technically sound publishing. Build for people first, and the machines follow.

MORE INSIGHTS

## How Do We Choose an Enterprise Architecture Tool in 2026?

URL: https://arithim.com/insight-how-to-choose-an-enterprise-architecture-tool.html

Insights / Enterprise architecture

# How Do We Choose an Enterprise Architecture Tool in 2026?

EA · RESEARCH·23 OCT 2026·7 MIN READ·BY TARUN BULCHANDANI

Most enterprise architecture tools can now model capabilities, applications and roadmaps well, so modelling features rarely decide a purchase. The questions that separate them in 2026 are how the repository stays current without constant manual effort, how AI and applications are priced, whether your AI assistants and agents can query it, and where your data is hosted.

Enterprise architecture is the category closest to how we work at Arithim. This piece draws on Gartner's Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Architecture Tools, published on 13 October 2026, which evaluated 15 vendors.

## What changed in 2026

Gartner describes a market that shifted sharply over the past year. Vendors poured money into AI, several rebuilt their products, and acquisitions continued. Ardoq bought GraphLake and GBTEC bought Inverbis in June 2026, Bizzdesign launched its Unify platform in April, and ValueBlue renamed itself BlueDolphin.

Two of Gartner's observations matter most for buyers. The first is that more people now get architecture answers by asking a company-wide AI assistant than by opening the EA tool, which is pushing vendors from per-seat pricing toward consumption- and outcome-based pricing. Gartner warns that EA tools risk becoming back-end repositories as a result. The second is that some EA teams are building their own AI tools on coding platforms to replicate EA features, which Gartner flags as a source of unmanaged AI risk. We wrote about that pattern more broadly in how to secure vibe-coded apps.

Gartner also names constant manual maintenance as the core problem for EA teams, and says the ideal is a live view of the organisation's current state.

## The 15 vendors at a glance

{.note} Positions from Gartner's Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Architecture Tools, 13 October 2026. Pricing and deployment as described in the report; check current terms with each vendor.

VendorGartner positionMain pricing unitDeployment

ArdoqLeaderPer applicationSaaS (public or private cloud)

BizzdesignLeaderPer userSaaS or on-premises

BOC GroupLeaderPer userSaaS (hosted in continental Europe) or on-premises

Orbus SoftwareLeaderPer user plus platform feeSaaS; FedRAMP government edition

SAP LeanIXLeaderPer applicationSaaS

GBTECChallengerPer role or enterprise licenceSaaS or on-premises

ServiceNowChallengerPer application or unrestricted usersSaaS or on-premises

AvolutionVisionaryPer userSaaS or on-premises

BlueDolphinVisionaryPer userSaaS

Enterprise Architecture SolutionsVisionaryFlat subscription; free open-source editionSaaS or on-premises

ins-piVisionaryPer product plus per userRuns on the ServiceNow platform

QualiWareVisionaryPer userSaaS or on-premises

Bee360Niche PlayerShare of managed IT budget, unlimited usersSaaS, private cloud or on-premises

Sparx SystemsNiche PlayerPer userSaaS or on-premises

UNICOM SystemsNiche PlayerPer user, unlimited read-only usersOn-premises or customer-managed only

Gartner is explicit that a Leader is not automatically the right choice, and that a more focused vendor can fit a particular industry, budget or feature need better.

## Five questions to ask before you buy

### 1. How will the repository stay current?

An EA tool is only trusted while its content is accurate. Most EA tools rely on integrations with the CMDB, project portfolio, finance and process tools, and Gartner points out that their value depends on data access and quality across those systems. ServiceNow and ins-pi avoid much of the integration work because they sit on the ServiceNow platform and read its CMDB directly, while the other vendors maintain connectors. Ask each vendor to show you how a new application, a retired one and a change of owner flow into the repository without someone typing them in.

### 2. How is AI priced, and will that price hold?

AI pricing varies more than anything else in this market. Ardoq and GBTEC include AI without metering. BOC Group, ins-pi, Sparx, QualiWare and Bee360 let you bring your own model API key. BlueDolphin uses a shared credit pool, SAP LeanIX uses SAP AI Units, ServiceNow uses Now Assist credits, Bizzdesign charges consumption fees through Unify, Orbus caps tokens and Avolution offers a monthly allowance. Gartner warns that vendors absorbing inference costs may come under margin pressure as agent workloads grow, so read the contract language on future AI features carefully.

### 3. Can your AI assistants and agents query it?

If people increasingly ask an enterprise AI assistant instead of opening the EA tool, the tool has to answer those questions through a standard interface. Gartner says buyers now see Model Context Protocol (MCP) access as essential. It notes that SAP LeanIX has shipped interactive MCP apps and Bee360 offers a vendor-managed MCP server, while Orbus trails most peers on customer-accessible MCP.

### 4. Does the pricing unit fit your scope?

Per-application pricing is easy to budget for application portfolio management, and Gartner cautions that it can discourage modelling the wider business. Per-user pricing can limit who gets access. Unlimited-user models (Bee360, Enterprise Architecture Solutions, and UNICOM's read-only users) suit organisations that want architecture content widely read.

### 5. Where will your data live?

For UK and EU buyers this often decides the shortlist. Many vendors in this market are European. BOC Group hosts its SaaS only in continental Europe, QualiWare offers content for NIS2, DORA and CSRD, and ins-pi is developing an AI model that keeps data inside your environment. Orbus has a FedRAMP-certified edition for US government. UNICOM offers no vendor-hosted option at all, and about 90% of QualiWare's customers still run on-premises.

## Our view: the repository matters more than the diagrams

Gartner's warning that EA tools could become back-end repositories reads to us like a description of where the value is heading. When agents start making changes across a business, they need an accurate map of which applications exist, what each one does, who owns it and what depends on it. The EA repository is the obvious place for that map. A tool that keeps its repository accurate and exposes it cleanly to AI will matter more in three years than one with the best modelling canvas.

That makes data freshness and open access the selection criteria we would weight most heavily, ahead of notation support or visualisation.

## Where agents help

Keeping the repository current is the job we think agents should take on first. An agent can compare the EA repository against the systems that actually change: the CMDB, cloud accounts, the single sign-on application list, software contracts and spend, and change tickets in ServiceNow or Jira. It can then propose updates, such as a new application found in SSO logs or an owner who has left, for an architect to approve in the EA tool itself. Over time it can flag drift between what the roadmap says and what is being built.

This works with whichever EA tool you already own, provided it has a usable API or MCP server. The architect still decides what goes into the repository; the agent takes over the data entry that most architects would happily give up.

## Common questions

### What is an enterprise architecture tool?

An EA tool is a central repository and modelling environment that records how an organisation's capabilities, processes, applications, information and technology relate to each other. Architects use it to analyse change, build roadmaps and test scenarios, and it connects to systems such as the CMDB, project portfolio and finance tools.

### Which enterprise architecture tools are Leaders in Gartner's 2026 Magic Quadrant?

In the October 2026 Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Architecture Tools, Gartner placed Ardoq, Bizzdesign, BOC Group, Orbus Software and SAP LeanIX in the Leaders quadrant. GBTEC and ServiceNow are Challengers; Avolution, BlueDolphin, Enterprise Architecture Solutions, ins-pi and QualiWare are Visionaries; and Bee360, Sparx Systems and UNICOM Systems are Niche Players. Gartner notes that a Leader is not always the right choice.

### How are enterprise architecture tools priced?

Mostly per application or per user. Ardoq, SAP LeanIX and ServiceNow price by application in most packages; most others price by user. Bee360 ties price to the share of IT budget managed, with unlimited users, and Enterprise Architecture Solutions offers a flat subscription and a free open-source edition. AI is priced separately in many cases, through credits, consumption fees or your own model API key.

### Is ServiceNow enough as an enterprise architecture tool?

It depends on what you need from EA. Gartner credits ServiceNow with a native, real-time repository built on its CMDB and with orchestration of AI agents across its products, but says its EA breadth trails the specialist vendors and its full value depends on other ServiceNow products. Organisations that are deep into ServiceNow and mainly need application portfolio management may find it enough.

### Can AI keep our architecture repository up to date?

Partly, and that is the most valuable use of AI in EA. Gartner says the biggest opportunity is ending constant manual maintenance and getting a live view of the current state. Agents can compare the repository against the CMDB, cloud accounts, single sign-on app lists, contracts and change tickets, and propose updates for an architect to approve. Data quality in those source systems still limits how far this goes.

## Sources

## How Do We Reduce Our Application Security Backlog?

URL: https://arithim.com/insight-how-to-reduce-application-security-backlog.html

Insights / Application security

# How Do We Reduce Our Application Security Backlog?

APPSEC · RESEARCH·22 OCT 2026·6 MIN READ·BY TARUN BULCHANDANI

Most application security backlogs shrink fastest when you cut the noise before anyone writes a fix, send every remaining finding to a named owner, and fix vulnerable dependencies in bulk. Generating patches is now the easy part, since most scanners can suggest one. What keeps backlogs large is the coordination around each fix, and that is where automation pays off.

This is the third piece in our application security series, after whether you need more than one AST tool and how to secure vibe-coded apps. It draws on Gartner's 2025 Magic Quadrant for Application Security Testing and its 2026 Magic Quadrant for Software Supply Chain Security.

## Why backlogs keep growing

Gartner's 2025 assessment of the AST market says that moving testing earlier in development, the long-running "shift left" effort, has largely been achieved, and that what now separates products is how they handle alert volume and remediation. Gartner also notes that AI coding assistants produce vulnerable code faster than developers can fix it, and it cites its own survey finding that 66% of organisations using AI in software development saw little or no improvement in code security.

The vendor profiles in Gartner's 2026 supply chain security report show the same pressure from the other side. Customers of several vendors reported large alert volumes and scan results that needed a lot of manual effort to work through, and some products need careful, ongoing policy tuning before their output is usable.

So the backlog is rarely caused by a lack of scanning. It grows because findings arrive from several tools, overlap, sit with no clear owner, and wait for someone to coordinate a fix.

## 1. Measure what matters

Before changing anything, break the backlog down by application, owning team, age, severity and source tool. Then add two questions for each finding. Is the vulnerable code reachable in the running application? Is the vulnerability being exploited, or likely to be? CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog answers the first part of that for public CVEs, and FIRST's Exploit Prediction Scoring System estimates the likelihood for the rest.

The number worth tracking is the count of reachable, likely-exploited findings, along with how long they've been open. Total finding count goes up every time you add a scanner, so it tells you very little.

## 2. Cut the noise before anyone writes a fix

Deduplicate findings that two or three tools report under different names. Set aside findings in code that never runs, in test fixtures, or in dependencies that are present but never called, and record the reason and a review date for each. Tune the rules that produce the most false positives. We would expect this step alone to remove a large share of most queues without any code changing.

## 3. Give every finding an owner

Findings without an owner tend to sit untouched. Map each repository and service to a team using code ownership files and a service catalogue such as Backstage or your CMDB, and route findings to that team's normal work queue. Findings that can't be matched to an owner go to a short weekly review, where someone assigns them or decides the code should be retired.

## 4. Fix dependencies in bulk

In many backlogs, a large share of findings come from open-source dependencies, and one upgrade can close dozens of them. Tools like Renovate and GitHub's Dependabot raise upgrade pull requests automatically. Some vendors go further; Gartner's 2026 report notes Mend.io's prediction of which version bumps will break a build and Sonatype's AI-assisted dependency upgrades. Grouping upgrades by application and merging them in regular batches gets through this part of the backlog much faster than handling findings one at a time.

## 5. Use autofix for code findings, with review

For findings in your own code, most leading scanners now generate a suggested patch. Gartner names Copilot Autofix, Veracode Fix, Snyk's fix automation, Checkmarx's assistant and Black Duck Assist among them. Treat these as drafts. A developer who knows the code should review each one, and the rescan should confirm the finding is gone before the ticket closes.

## 6. Set deadlines by risk, and stop the backlog refilling

Set fix deadlines by risk tier, shortest for exploited vulnerabilities in internet-facing systems. Allow exceptions, but give each one a named approver and an expiry date. Then make sure new code doesn't add to the pile. A pipeline check that blocks new critical findings, while leaving existing ones to the backlog process, keeps the queue from growing back while you work it down.

## Where agents help

Steps three to six are mostly coordination. Someone has to find the owner, open the ticket, nudge the reviewer, re-run the scan, close the ticket and report progress, for every finding, across every tool. That work suits an agent well.

Gartner's 2026 supply chain report says GitHub has not yet shipped fully autonomous agentic workflows for security backlogs and pull requests, while some competitors already offer them. Those vendor agents work inside each vendor's own product. Most organisations run several scanners, so the coordination across them, together with the ticketing system and the people involved, is still left to someone on the security team.

The agent we would build for this picks up prioritised findings from every scanner, routes each to its owner, drafts or requests the fix, opens the pull request, follows up with reviewers, confirms the rescan and closes the ticket. A person approves every merge, and every decision the agent makes is logged with its reasoning. We describe it alongside the other agents in our application security research.

## Common questions

### Why does our security backlog keep growing even though we scan everything?

Scanning finds problems faster than most teams can fix them, and AI coding tools have widened that gap by producing more code. Gartner's 2025 Magic Quadrant for Application Security Testing says the hard part of the market has moved from finding issues to managing alert volume and remediation. If findings aren't deduplicated, routed to an owner and tracked to a merged fix, the backlog grows by default.

### Should we close findings in code that isn't reachable?

Don't delete them, but take them out of the queue people work from. Record why each one was set aside and when it should be looked at again, so an auditor can follow the decision and the finding comes back if the code path changes.

### Can AI fix our security backlog automatically?

It can write many of the fixes. GitHub Copilot Autofix, Veracode Fix, Snyk and Checkmarx all generate patches, and tools like Renovate and Dependabot automate dependency upgrades. A person still needs to review and merge each change, and someone has to route the work, chase reviews and confirm the rescan is clean. That coordination is where most of the time goes.

### What should we measure to know the backlog is improving?

Track open findings that are both reachable and likely to be exploited, their age, and the median time from detection to merged fix for each team. Total finding count is a poor measure, because it rises every time you add a scanner.

### What is a reasonable fix deadline for a critical vulnerability?

It depends on whether the vulnerability is known to be exploited and whether the affected code is exposed. Many organisations use days for critical issues that appear in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on internet-facing systems, and weeks or months for issues with no known exploit in internal code. Set the deadlines by risk tier and allow time-limited exceptions with a named approver.

## How Do I Secure Our CI/CD Pipelines and GitHub Actions?

URL: https://arithim.com/insight-how-to-secure-ci-cd-pipelines-github-actions.html

Insights / Application security

# How Do I Secure Our CI/CD Pipelines and GitHub Actions?

APPSEC · RESEARCH·24 OCT 2026·5 MIN READ·BY TARUN BULCHANDANI

Start by taking an inventory: every pipeline, every runner, every secret it can reach and every third-party action or plugin it pulls in. Then pin third-party actions to exact commits, cut each workflow's token permissions to the minimum, replace stored cloud keys with short-lived credentials, and sign what you build. Most organisations have never done the inventory, which is why pipelines have become an easy way in.

This is part of our application security series, alongside whether you need more than one AST tool and how to reduce your security backlog.

## Why pipelines became a target

Two incidents in 2025 showed how much damage a pipeline compromise can do. In March, the widely used GitHub Action tj-actions/changed-files was compromised, and, according to CISA's alert, the malicious code exposed secrets from the workflows that used it, including cloud access keys, GitHub personal access tokens, npm tokens and private keys. In September, a self-spreading worm called Shai-Hulud compromised more than 500 npm packages. CISA reported that it stole GitHub tokens and cloud API keys from developers and used their npm access to publish infected versions of other packages.

Both attacks worked because build systems hold powerful credentials and run third-party code that few people review.

## What the research says about the tools

Pipeline security is the weakest area in most application security tooling. In Gartner's 2025 Critical Capabilities for Application Security Testing, it had the lowest median score of the 15 capabilities rated across 16 vendors. Gartner's 2026 Magic Quadrant for Software Supply Chain Security lists several vendors with no pipeline posture checks at all. A few focus on the problem: Gartner credits OX Security with pipeline posture management through its Pipeline Bill of Materials, and notes that Cycode released runtime pipeline protection after the Shai-Hulud attack. GitHub is credited with attestations and branch protections in Actions.

Gartner's 2026 Hype Cycle for Secure Software Engineering adds two practical observations. Many organisations collect software bills of materials without having decided how to evaluate, store or use them, and signing and verifying artifacts in CI/CD is still awkward for developers.

## A hardening checklist

These steps apply to GitHub Actions specifically, and most have direct equivalents in GitLab CI, Azure DevOps and Jenkins.

### Take an inventory

List every repository with a pipeline, every runner (hosted and self-hosted), every secret each workflow can read, and every third-party action, plugin or container image it uses. Tools such as OpenSSF Scorecard can check many of these settings across repositories automatically. Without this list, the rest of the checklist can't be applied consistently.

### Pin third-party actions to commits

A version tag like v4 can be moved to different code, which is how the tj-actions compromise reached so many workflows. GitHub's guidance recommends pinning third-party actions to a full-length commit SHA. Use a dependency bot to propose updates, so pinning doesn't leave you stuck on old versions.

### Cut token permissions to the minimum

Set the default GITHUB_TOKEN permission to read-only at the organisation level, and grant write access only in the workflows and jobs that need it. Be careful with triggers that run untrusted code with elevated permissions, such as pull_request_target on public repositories.

### Replace stored cloud keys with short-lived credentials

Use OpenID Connect so each job requests a short-lived credential from AWS, Azure or Google Cloud, scoped to that repository and environment. A stolen short-lived token is worth far less than a cloud key that never expires.

### Protect runners and deployments

Use ephemeral runners that are destroyed after each job, and never run self-hosted runners for public repositories. Put production deployments behind environments that require a named reviewer, and protect workflow files with code ownership so changes to them get a security review.

### Sign what you build

Generate provenance for every artifact you ship. GitHub's artifact attestations and the open-source Sigstore project make this much easier than it used to be, and the SLSA framework gives you levels to aim for. Verify signatures at deployment, otherwise signing proves little.

### Scan for secrets and keep scanning

Turn on secret scanning and push protection on every repository, and rotate any credential that has ever appeared in a log or a commit. After the 2025 incidents, CISA's advice included rotating developer credentials and requiring phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication.

## Where agents help

The checklist itself is not hard. Keeping hundreds of repositories compliant with it, as teams add workflows every week, is. That makes it a good job for an agent. A pipeline auditor agent can read every workflow across GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins and Azure DevOps, score each one against your policy and SLSA, and open pull requests with the fixes: pinning actions, trimming permissions, switching to OIDC. A person reviews and merges each change, and the agent reports drift as new workflows appear.

Because so few application security tools cover pipelines well, this is one of the clearer gaps we found in our research on the AST market, and one of the first agents we would build.

## Common questions

### What is CI/CD pipeline security?

It is the protection of the systems that build, test and deploy your software: the pipeline definitions, the runners that execute them, the secrets they use, and the third-party actions, plugins and packages they pull in. Attackers target pipelines because one compromised step can steal credentials or insert malicious code into everything the pipeline ships.

### Why should we pin GitHub Actions to a commit SHA?

A version tag such as v4 can be moved to point at different code, which is what happened when the tj-actions/changed-files action was compromised in March 2025. GitHub's security guidance recommends pinning third-party actions to a full-length commit SHA, so a workflow only runs the exact code you reviewed.

### How do we stop pipelines leaking cloud credentials?

Stop storing long-lived cloud keys as pipeline secrets. GitHub Actions and most CI systems support OpenID Connect, which lets a workflow request a short-lived credential from AWS, Azure or Google Cloud for a single job. Combine that with minimal token permissions per workflow and secret scanning on every repository.

### Do application security tools cover pipeline security?

Mostly not yet. In Gartner's 2025 Critical Capabilities for Application Security Testing, pipeline security was the weakest capability across 16 vendors, and Gartner's 2026 Magic Quadrant for Software Supply Chain Security lists several vendors with no pipeline posture checks at all. A few vendors, including OX Security and Cycode, focus on it.

### What is SLSA, and do we need it?

SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts) is an open framework that defines levels of build integrity, such as recording signed provenance for every artifact. It is a useful target for any organisation that ships software to customers, and regulations such as the EU Cyber Resilience Act are pushing in the same direction.

Complimentary reprints; links may expire.

## How Do I Secure Vibe-Coded Apps Built by People Who Aren't Developers?

URL: https://arithim.com/insight-how-to-secure-vibe-coded-apps.html

Insights / Application security

# How Do I Secure Vibe-Coded Apps Built by People Who Aren't Developers?

APPSEC · RESEARCH·21 OCT 2026·6 MIN READ·BY TARUN BULCHANDANI

Treat them like any other application your company runs. Find them, give each one a named owner, scan them with the same tools you use on the rest of your code, and decide which of them are allowed near customer data. Most of these apps never pass through the systems where a security team would normally catch problems, which is why they need a process of their own.

This piece follows our look at whether you need more than one application security testing tool. It draws on Gartner's Hype Cycle for Secure Software Engineering, 2026 and its 2025 Magic Quadrant for Application Security Testing, plus what the tool vendors offer today.

## Why vibe-coded apps are a security problem

A finance analyst who builds an invoice tracker with an AI app builder has done something useful, but none of the usual checks happened along the way. Nobody reviewed the code, nobody scanned the open-source packages the AI chose, the database password is probably sitting in the source, and the app may be on the public internet because that was the default.

Gartner's 2026 Hype Cycle for Secure Software Engineering says this directly. Vibe-coded prototypes can reach production without security checks, coding agents can pull in vulnerable or malicious packages, and the MCP servers those agents connect to can have access nobody approved. Gartner's 2025 Magic Quadrant for Application Security Testing cites its own survey finding that 66% of organisations using AI tools in software development saw little or no improvement in code security. An independent study from Georgetown's Center for Security and Emerging Technology found that almost half of the code samples produced by five AI models contained bugs, many of them exploitable.

A developer who sees a scanner finding can usually judge whether it's serious. Someone who builds apps from a finance or operations role can't, and shouldn't have to.

## Where these apps tend to live

Common places to find them include:

repositories in personal GitHub or GitLab accounts, often created with a work email address

apps deployed straight from an AI app builder to its own hosting, on a subdomain the company doesn't control

internal tools running on a laptop or a spare cloud account outside the landing zone

low-code apps and automations connected to company SaaS through personal API tokens

MCP servers and coding-agent configurations on individual machines

None of these show up in the tools a security team normally watches, because those tools only see code that someone has put into a governed repository and pipeline.

## A practical process

### 1. Find them

Start with the signals you already have. Single sign-on and OAuth grant logs show which AI builders people have connected to company accounts. Expense and card data shows who is paying for them. DNS and certificate records show new subdomains. Your source control admin console shows repositories created outside the main organisation, and network logs show traffic to AI coding services. Several application security vendors now offer discovery of AI assets as well, which helps with code that is already in a repository.

### 2. Give each app an owner and a tier

For every app you find, record who uses it, what data it touches and who can reach it. Then place it in a tier, such as prototype, internal tool or business-critical. The tier decides how much scrutiny it gets. A prototype that only its builder uses needs a quick scan and a reminder. An app that holds customer records needs the same review as anything else that holds customer records.

### 3. Scan it like any other code

Move the code into a repository your scanners cover and run the same static analysis, dependency checks and secrets scanning you run everywhere else. For anything above prototype, also check that login actually works the way the owner thinks it does, and run a dynamic scan against the deployed app. Gartner recommends keeping traditional SAST and SCA tools alongside AI code assistants, and we agree. Some newer tools, such as Semgrep Guardian and OX Security's VibeSec, check code while an AI agent is writing it, which helps for builders whose tools support them.

### 4. Explain the findings in plain language

A finding like "SQL injection in search.py, line 42" means nothing to most app builders. "Anyone who types this into the search box can read every customer record" does. For each finding, explain what an attacker could do, and give the owner a fix they can apply. Often the most useful fix is a prompt they can paste back into the AI tool that wrote the code, followed by a rescan to confirm it worked.

### 5. Make the safe route the easy one

Gartner's advice for secure development generally is to make security the path of least resistance, and it fits here. Approve a short list of AI builders behind single sign-on. Provide templates with login, secrets handling and logging already done. Give coding agents the minimum permissions they need, which Gartner calls "least agency", and require a human review before anything high-risk goes live.

## Why a ban rarely works

Banning AI app builders is the obvious response, and it usually backfires. The people building these apps are solving real problems, and a ban moves their work onto personal accounts and credit cards where you have even less visibility. A short approved list with good templates gets you more control.

## Where an agent helps

Most of this process is repetitive coordination. Someone has to watch the discovery signals, open a record for each new app, ask the builder a few questions, run the scans, translate the results and chase the fix. We think an intake agent can do most of that. It would pick up a new app from the logs, message the builder in Slack or Teams to confirm ownership and purpose, run the scans, and write up each finding in plain language with a suggested fix. A person on the security team would still approve any move to the business-critical tier.

This is one of the agents we described in our application security research. As far as we can see, no vendor covers it end to end yet. Several discover AI assets, but finding an app is only the first step.

## Common questions

### What is vibe coding?

Vibe coding is building software by describing what you want to an AI tool in plain language and accepting the code it produces, often without reading it closely. It lets people with no development background build working apps in an afternoon.

### Are vibe-coded apps less secure than apps written by developers?

Often, yes, mainly because they skip the checks developer code goes through. Gartner's 2026 research warns that vibe-coded prototypes can reach production without any security review, and a 2024 Georgetown CSET study found that almost half of the code samples produced by five AI models contained bugs, many of them exploitable.

### Should we ban AI app builders?

We don't recommend it. A ban tends to push the work onto personal accounts and credit cards, where you can't see it at all. Approving a small set of tools, behind single sign-on, with templates that already handle login and secrets, gives people a safer route that's also the easier one.

### Which tools check AI-generated code for vulnerabilities?

Your existing SAST, SCA and secrets scanners work on AI-generated code once it's in a repository they cover. Some newer tools check code as an AI agent writes it, such as Semgrep Guardian and OX Security's VibeSec. Gartner recommends keeping traditional SAST and SCA alongside AI code assistants.

### Who should own a vibe-coded app?

The person or team that uses it should be its named business owner, responsible for keeping it patched or retiring it. Security sets the rules and runs the scans; the owner answers for what the app does with company data.

## Sources
